reason: The speed numbers are exactly what I care about, so I'd install it and throw a few hundred RAWs at it. But it's one dev, version 0.4.1, and nothing in the post says it's signed or open source, so I'm not making it the thing that opens every file I double-click.
why_switch_or_not: Next/back at 40-50 ms and rapid-next x5 at 85 ms would genuinely matter when I'm culling RAW+JPG, and showing RAW and JPG as separate pictures is how I want it. But the post doesn't say whether the RAW developer or the embedded preview is the default, whether I can rate or flag and then filter, or whether it handles my camera's RAW files, and those are what I need for culling. Setting it as default means ticking every format by hand in Windows Settings, and if it chokes on one RAW I lose a cull session. The benchmark is also the developer's own, on one PC at 2560x1440.
current_app_pros: Windows Photos is already there and opens on double-click with no setup. It's reliable and I never have to think about it.
current_app_pains: It's slow to open and slow when I hold the arrow key through a shoot, which I notice every time. It shows RAW poorly, mostly relying on the codec and the embedded preview. It's useless for culling because it has no real rating or compare view. That's why I already use a separate culling tool for the real work.
objection: Is an unknown .exe from one developer safe? There's no mention of code signing or open source, and I'm not putting that on every file I open until I know.
would_change_my_mind: A signed installer, or open source I can check, plus a clean test on my own RAW+JPG shoots where it stays as fast as the benchmark says and doesn't misread colour.
